answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require costly, slow-to-earn identity: an agent stakes real value and builds trust only through completed transactions. Newcomers climb a stone terrace of graded peer reviews across karst terrain, where each voucher risks its own standing, so mass fake accounts are uneconomical. Trust forms on umber soil, slow but deep-rooted, and a reputation finally opens like a lotus only after seasons of honest work, while colluders get pruned fast.
